On 29 June 1939, after a referendum, the legislature voted to dissolve the state and join Turkey. Critics called the referendum rigged, because Turkey reportedly brought in tens of thousands of Turks from outside to register and vote.

On 29 June 1939 the legislature voted unanimously to dissolve the state and join Turkey. Sources differ on whether the public voted first. Wikipedia's articles on the state and on the dispute say a referendum came before the decision and give it no date of its own. The article on the state, citing the journalist Robert Fisk, reports that it was called phoney and rigged, because Turkey brought in tens of thousands of Turks from outside to register and vote. A 2020 article by Mevlüt Çelebi in a Turkish history journal describes the elections to the assembly in 1938 and the assembly's unanimous decision, and it mentions no public vote. Whether a separate referendum was held in 1939 is not known.

story: Until 2010 the zone covered four districts totalling 493 square kilometres, and in 2010 it was extended to the rest of the city.

Until 2010 the zone covered four districts, Luohu, Futian, Nanshan and Yantian. Sources give different areas for it. One chronology gives 327.5 square kilometres at its founding in August 1980, the South China Morning Post gave 395 just before the expansion, and Wikipedia gives 493 for the four districts. On 1 July 2010 it was extended to the whole city, which the South China Morning Post put at 1,948 square kilometres.

story: King Zog of Albania lived in London and then nearby from April 1939, but the Allies refused to recognise him or work with him, and he abdicated in 1946.

King Zog of Albania fled the Italian invasion of April 1939 and lived in England during the war, but the Allies refused to recognise him or work with him. Accounts differ on how his title ended in 1946. Britannica says he formally abdicated on 2 January, while other accounts say Albania's new government formally deposed him that day.

story: The settlement was abolished in 1943 and the Chinese Nationalists took it back.

After the Pacific War began in 1941, Japanese forces occupied Kulangsu, restructured the Municipal Council and expelled foreigners of other countries, though one account dates the occupation to 1942. Treaties signed by Chiang Kai-shek's government ended foreign privileges in China in 1943, the year Wikipedia gives for the settlement's end. The Japanese occupation lasted until 1945. The Chinese Nationalists took the island back, on a date that is not known, and Communist forces took it in October 1949.

The men of this advance party were sentenced to 34 years in jail.

In November 2004 a court in Equatorial Guinea sentenced du Toit to 34 years in jail and four other South Africans to 17 years each, and it acquitted three South Africans. The Armenian defendants received 14 or 24 years, with accounts differing on how many got each term. Moto, tried in his absence, received 63 years, and eight members of his government in exile received 52 years each. Prosecutors had asked for the death penalty for du Toit and Moto, and the court imposed none. Amnesty International called the trial seriously flawed, citing confessions said to have been obtained under torture. A German detainee, Gerhard Merz, died in prison nine days after the arrests. The authorities gave cerebral malaria as the cause, and two defendants testified that torture killed him.
